title: The state glyph on a workspace card looks like the button it is
body:
A workspace's card in the open sidebar draws its agent's state as a line: a glyph from `mark`, the agent's name, the state's label and its age (`draw_card` and the state line in `src/server/chrome/frame.rs`). A click on the glyph clears `done` and `attention` to idle (`Hit::Clear` from `Frame::hit`). The glyph is one cell of text at the start of the line, and `Frame::hover` reports a hover over it as a hover over the whole card. Jack did not know it could be clicked. decade-ca56f2 asked for a redesign.

## Proposal

- The glyph is bigger than one text cell.
- The glyph stands apart from the card's status lines, in its own place on the card rather than as the first character of the state line.
- The glyph looks like a button on hover. `Frame::hover` reports it as its own target, and decade draws a hover state on it that is distinct from the card's own hover.
- A click still gives `Hit::Clear`, and only for `done` and `attention`.

## Open

- Where on the card the glyph sits, and how big it is.
- What the hover looks like, and whether it shows what a click does, such as a check mark.
- Whether the glyph still shows for `working` and `idle`, where a click does nothing.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/7403d304
notes.text: To be built together with the breathing card chosen in decade-8d1fa9.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/7403d304
notes.text: Jack chose variant B from the second prototype (tmp-claude/2026-11-10-card-blink/glyphs2.html): a disc about 26 px across at the card's top-right, spanning its first two rows, holding the state glyph. On hover over an attention or done disc, a ring appears and the glyph turns into a check mark. Working and idle show the disc with no hover. Row 2 stops short of the disc. The card no longer shows a tab count at all; Jack wants it removed.
